ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, objects A and B are connected with a light string and a spring and then pass over a pulley. A is at rest on a rough inclined plane with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$, and B is hanging. It is known that the mass mA＝3mB, and pulley friction is neglected. Now the inclination angle of the inclined plane is decreased from $45^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$, and A always remains at rest relative to the inclined plane. Then which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The static friction force on object A will decrease

A is at rest on a rough inclined plane with an inclination angle of $45^{\circ}$, and B is hanging. It is known that the mass mA=3mB, and pulley friction is neglected. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, object A is placed on an inclined plane slanting upward to the right, and the inclined plane angle is labeled as 45°; A is connected, through a spring in the upward direction along the inclined plane and a light string passing over the fixed pulley at the upper right, to object B hanging on the right. Therefore the pulling force of the spring/string on A is upward along the inclined plane, and B hangs vertically to provide the tension in the string. Then reason: B is hanging at rest and the pulley has no friction, so the magnitude of the pulling force transmitted in the string to the spring and acting on A is T=m_B g. Write the equilibrium equation for A along the inclined-plane direction: the component of A's gravity downward along the inclined plane is m_A g\sin\theta=3m_B g\sin\theta, and the pulling force T is upward along the inclined plane. Compare the two angles: when \theta=45^\circ, 3m_B g\sin45^\circ>m_B g; when \theta=30^\circ, 3m_B g\sin30^\circ>m_B g. Therefore in both cases A has a tendency to slide downward along the inclined plane, and the static friction force is upward along the inclined plane in both cases. Its magnitude is f=3m_B g\sin\theta-m_B g. Initially f_1=3m_B g\sin45^\circ-m_B g, later f_2=3m_B g\sin30^\circ-m_B g. Since \sin45^\circ>\sin30^\circ, f_2<f_1.
